title: INT8 weight-only failure-mode injection & sensitivity harness for GPTQ/AWQ profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a deterministic regression harness that injects realistic failure modes and sensitivity perturbations to validate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles across our CI and nightly regression pipelines. This work focuses on calibration drift cases, edge-case prompts, sequence-length distribution shifts, and numeric stability scenarios that previously surfaced in production canaries. The harness will be integrated with the profile registry, produce per-run fidelity metrics against golden answers, and emit structured telemetry tags so Console dashboards and Optimize tooling can detect regressions and recommend rollbacks or alternative profiles.
acceptance_criteria: New harness runs in CI (presubmit) and nightly regression with <=12h extra runtime on nightly runner
Injectable failure modes: clipping of KV cache, simulated quantization noise, outlier activation scaling, and reduced mantissa emulation for FP8/INT8 mixed profiles
Per-profile fidelity metrics (ROUGE/L1/answer-exact-match where applicable) are computed and stored in the profile registry and linked to each run
Automated drift detector flags runs when fidelity drop > configurable threshold and opens ENG or PM issues automatically
Backward-compatibility check: any profile rolling to canary must pass sensitivity sweep on 5 representative models and two sequence-length distributions
Console dashboard tile shows trendline and tagged runs for quick triage; alerting configured for P1 regression
Run artifacts (log, sample inputs/outputs, seed, binary diffs) are archived to the nightly bucket for 90 days

notes: This harness is intentionally conservative for presubmit (fast checks) and more exhaustive at nightly frequency.
Plan to include sample prompt corpus from real-product telemetry after privacy review; initially use synthetic and public datasets.
Consider toggling AWQ vs GPTQ paths via registry flags to aid canary rollouts.
